reading_rules: The numbers are committed before any candidate run. Only the owner can loosen one, in writing, and never the engineer who missed it.
The blind hold-out is the only honest number and does not exist until E0 ends; it is read once, at the end.

Every gate states its n beside it and is reported with a bootstrap interval clustered by conversation or case, and with a rater-disagreement sensitivity (relevant only against relevant plus marginal).
A rate gate is set and read on the dev sets (the 400 research negatives, the 300 controls, the typo and messy dev sets); 20 messages in one language cannot carry a rate (one error in 20 is 5%).
A 'no worse than baseline' gate is paired and one-sided (no query loses a relevant paper; no more than k right-to-wrong), not an absolute number copied from the in-sample baseline.
A margin is set above the in-sample value and never at it (a limit equal to the in-sample rate is failed about half the time by chance on a fresh set).

With n error-free cases an upper bound of about 3/n at 95% is all that can be claimed: 0 of 100 at most about 3%, 0 of 250 about 1.2%, 0 of 300 about 1%; an observed 2 of 100 at most about 7%, 3 of 100 about 8%.
Provider answers move run to run (15 and 16 of 20 papers the same on repeats), so replay is the gate and live runs are the drift alarm.
The sign test on the 113 follow-ups is one-sided: 6 worse and 0 better gives p = 0.016, 6 and 1 gives 0.063, 5 and 1 gives 0.109.
A rate is read on the dev set with its interval and the sealed hold-out is read once, at the end (4.0, line 206).

kinds.rate_max: observed k events of n cases; passes when k/n is at most threshold; needs n >= n_min
kinds.rate_min: observed k successes of n cases; passes when k/n is at least threshold; needs n >= n_min
kinds.paired_no_worse: observed worse, better and n pairs; passes when worse is at most threshold (the most cases that may get worse); the one-sided exact sign-test p is reported; needs n >= n_min
kinds.count_equals: observed count (and n); passes when the count equals threshold; needs n >= n_min where one is given
kinds.floor: observed value (and n, and reference for a relative limit); direction at_least (>=), at_most (<=) or under (<) against threshold, or against reference + threshold when relative_to is set
kinds.tests_pass: observed passed and failed; passes when none failed and at least n_min (or one) ran; threshold is null
kinds.report_only: reported with its n and interval, never passes or fails (a target the plan calls 'not a gate', or a number with no rule)
